answer: Proof-of-replication resists sybils: each identity must prove it stores a UNIQUE physically-distinct encoding of a dataset, not a shared or deduplicated copy, re-challenged on a pulse. A farm cannot back a thousand identities with one ivory disk because the proof forces each replica to be independently encoded — velvet-smooth deduplication is detected and rejected. Honest agents each hold one genuine replica; a swarm needs genuinely separate physical storage per head, a cost that does not collapse onto shared hardware.
